## AI Skills System Overview and Implementation

Franz provided Malia with a comprehensive walkthrough of the AI skills system, detailing how skills are structured, discovered, and utilized within GitHub Copilot and Claude, including the creation, organization, and runtime behavior of skills for various use cases.

### Skills Structure and Discovery

Franz explained that skills are defined as markdown files placed in either a global user folder or a repository-specific folder, allowing for both personal and project-specific customization. Skills are discovered at runtime based on their location, and users must opt into agent skills in settings to enable specialized capabilities for chat requests.

### Context Management and Limitations

Franz described the importance of context memory in AI interactions, noting that MCP tools immediately consume context space, which is limited. Skills, however, only use context when invoked, allowing hundreds of skills to be available without overloading the system's memory.

### Skill Usage and API Integration

Franz demonstrated how invoking a skill, such as the Cortex skill, enables the AI to interact with APIs (e.g., listing teams or team members) using secure environment variables for authentication, and highlighted the process for updating and improving skills based on usage feedback.

### Skill Evolution and Optimization

Franz discussed the iterative improvement of skills, including self-reflection and embedding fixes directly into skill files, as well as the existence of a skill optimizer to retrofit enhancements across multiple skills for consistency and context optimization.
